name: synthesis-scenario-add-coupon-checkout
query: i need to repro a registered shopper adding a promo coupon to their basket and checking out -- on an instance. which SCAPI calls do i need in what order, and which scopes must the SLAS client have
hypothesis: Multi-call SCAPI plan must surface addCouponToBasket as the named coupon operation (verified in spec at shopper-baskets/addCouponToBasket.json: POST /organizations/{organizationId}/baskets/{basketId}/coupons, scopes [sfcc.shopper-baskets-orders.rw, sfcc.shopper-standard]), thread basketId from createBasket through to checkout, and cite both shopper-baskets and shopper-orders public reference URLs. The combined-scope assertion uses an alternation (sfcc.shopper-baskets-orders.rw | sfcc.shopper-(baskets|orders)) so that whether the model surfaces the rolled-up RW scope or the per-reference fallbacks both render as a pass. Tool-path assertions deliberately omitted (see iteration-synthesis-assertion-relaxation in dsc-endpoint-help).

assertions.because: the named SCAPI operation for adding a coupon must appear in the plan (verified real op in shopper-baskets spec)
must cite the public shopper-baskets reference URL
must cite the public shopper-orders reference URL -- proves the multi-reference plan walks both
scope union must surface either the rolled-up baskets-orders.rw scope or the per-reference fallbacks (both are valid per the spec's accepted-scope list on addCouponToBasket and createOrder)

SLAS leg 1 must name a flow-correct operation. Either authenticateCustomer (registered-b2c flow, the OOTB-platform-IDP default) or authorizeCustomer (registered-federated flow). The fixture's prompt says 'registered shopper' without specifying federation, so the model should pick registered-b2c -> authenticateCustomer; this loosened assertion accepts either pick because both are spec-correct registered flows, but the new synthesis-scenario-registered-silent fixture below asserts authenticateCustomer strictly to guard the OOTB-platform-IDP default.

SLAS leg 2 must be explicitly named as the getAccessToken operation -- both legs are required to actually obtain the bearer token, and the plan must show them as separate expanded steps. Pairs with the authorizeCustomer assertion above; this tightening makes the assertion intent (full SLAS expansion) sharper than the prior reference-OR-leg regex.

PKCE bash must use the 96-byte form (yields the RFC-7636-max 128-char verifier) per the SKILL.md 'PKCE in the runnable' rule. The SKILL.md instructs the model to invoke scripts/pkce-snippet.js, which emits this exact form. Hand-rolled snippets drift toward the 32-byte / 43-char minimum form -- this assertion catches that regression. Tests outcome (the form ends up in the bash) rather than mechanism (whether the script was invoked or its content was inlined); both routes satisfy the spirit of the rule, only the byte count is what customers actually see.

must cite the SLAS reference's public DSC URL. The reference's URL slug on developer.salesforce.com is `auth` (page title is 'Shopper Login (SLAS)' but the URL is /references/auth, not /references/shopper-login -- /references/shopper-login 404s). The negative lookahead `(?![a-zA-Z0-9_-])` enforces a slug boundary, so /references/auth and /references/auth?meta=authorizeCustomer pass while /references/auth-admin, /references/authentication, and /guide/authorization-... do not.

must NOT use the shrug phrasings flagged in iteration-todo-slas-cross-reference-prose.md. SLAS is a DSC reference; calling a SLAS step 'external' or 'not part of' the reference set misrepresents the skill's universe to the user.
citation-leak guard -- local cache paths must never appear in customer-facing answers

auth-code capture must be headless for the guest and registered-B2C legs: both SLAS legs return the code in the 303 Location header, so a single curl captures it. A 'open this URL in a browser', 'paste the code', or read -rp prompt mid-script breaks the paste-and-run contract (see SKILL.md 'Capturing the authorization code in the runnable'). The registered-federated fixture is the deliberate exception and asserts the inverse.

the authorization code arrives in the 303 Location header, never a JSON response body -- neither authorizeCustomer nor authenticateCustomer declares a 200/JSON body or an authorizationCode field. Parsing the code out of a JSON body -- a property read like .authorizationCode / ['authorization_code'], or JSON.parse(resp).code against the authorize/login response -- is a fabricated response shape (see SKILL.md 'The code is in the Location header, never a JSON response body'). Matches only the parse construct, not the bare field name in prose, so an answer that *warns against* the JSON-body shape (e.g. 'read from the Location header, not a JSON authorizationCode field') still passes.

authenticateCustomer takes shopper credentials in a Basic auth header, not login_id/login_password form fields -- those are fabricated (the spec declares no such parameters). Matches login_id/login_password only as an actual form field, query param, or JSON key (--data-urlencode "login_id, [?&]login_id=, \"login_id\":, login_password=), NOT the bare token -- so an answer that *warns against* the fabrication ("no login_id/login_password form fields") still passes. Retuned in iteration-runnable-jq after the bare-token form false-flagged that warning prose.

the /login leg's required channel parameter is channel_id, not channel_type -- channel_type is a fabrication that appears when the model drops the real (required) channel_id. The spec's required params are code_challenge, channel_id, client_id, redirect_uri.

grant_type belongs on the /token exchange (getAccessToken), not on /login. Matches grant_type only when it follows oauth2/login within 200 chars AND no step/token boundary (/token, getAccessToken, 'Step ', '##', 'Exchange') intervenes -- so grant_type appearing in the very next step, or in a 'Why' line referencing getAccessToken, does not false-match. Retuned in iteration-runnable-jq after the prior 400-char window leaked across the step boundary into the legitimate getAccessToken step.

channel_id is a spec-required parameter on authenticateCustomer (description: 'Required parameters: code_challenge, channel_id, client_id, and redirect_uri'). It is easy to drop -- this guards that the registered-B2C login leg includes it. Verified: every transcript that omitted channel_id also carried another fabrication, so its absence is a real defect, not idiom variance.

the runnable must extract JSON response fields (access_token, basketId, etc.) with `jq -r`, the idiom the deterministic renderer (scripts/curl-block.js) emits -- not a hand-rolled `node -e "...JSON.parse..."` or `python3 -c "...json.load..."` stdin-reader, which is not what a support engineer pastes into a terminal (see SKILL.md 'Extracting JSON response fields in the runnable'). Scoped to the JSON-parse idiom, so the mandated `node <path>/pkce-snippet.js` invocation -- which has no -e and no JSON.parse -- does not match.

the runnable threads at least one field (access_token / basketId / shipping-method id) from one call's JSON response into the next, and must do it with `jq -r` -- matching scripts/curl-block.js. Pairs with the node -e/python3 exclude above.

query: Build me a scenario for the SCAPI Admin orders API: what are the prerequisites for `getOrder`? Which calls happen first, in what order, and what auth setup is needed?
hypothesis: SCAPI Admin orders endpoints declare AmOAuth2 -- pickAuthBranch routes to 'am' and the plan emits an AM auth step pointing at account.demandware.net/dwsso/oauth2/access_token with grant_type=client_credentials. The plan must NOT fabricate a developer.salesforce.com URL for AM (Salesforce keeps AM undocumented by design) and must NOT leak SLAS auth steps (authorizeCustomer / authenticateCustomer) because Admin endpoints don't accept SLAS tokens.

assertions.because: AM token endpoint is the canonical https://account.demandware.net/dwsso/oauth2/access_token. The skill hardcodes this URL; the plan must cite it verbatim.
AM flow default is private client + grant_type=client_credentials.
the AM client must be configured with the orders scope -- either bare sfcc.orders (read-sufficient for getOrder) or sfcc.orders.rw.
AM has no DSC reference page (deliberate by Salesforce). The plan must NOT fabricate a developer.salesforce.com URL for AM.
Admin orders endpoints declare AmOAuth2, not ShopperToken; the plan must NOT include SLAS auth steps.
citation-leak guard.
